g.title: ingress
g.text: 2 · North-south — how a request reaches a service
three trust-zone Gateways with independent public, private and tailnet DNS paths; instantiated identically in every cluster

g.text: Clients, and the zones they resolve

or s3 sub-tiers and no WebRTC,

g.text: wildcards, HTTP on :80 and Forgejo SSH
listener is removed; DNS is a separate

g.title: g_envoy
g.text: Three GatewayClasses per cluster, each with its own
EnvoyProxy — but the one for home-ts is named ts.
Gateways public and private whole, and wildcard-ts
covers Gateway ts whole. The Gateways themselves
are defined ONCE, in apps/base/home, and reused

g.title: p_dns
g.text: plus one for keiretsu.top that reads

g.title: r_dist
g.text: private and ts together are the default for admin
consoles. A handful of user-facing apps add public.
The CDN tier is public only, and rewrites the Host
Three separate dashboard deployments share one

g.title: s_dns
g.text: suffix at its local k8gb CoreDNS
there is no shared tailnet zone.

g.title: r_listener
g.text: Check the listeners before adding a route
A route whose hostname matches no listener reports
nothing. The three tiers do not carry the same
hostname sets, so confirm against the live Gateway

g.title: r_trap
g.text: A ${CLUSTER_DOMAIN} route gets DNS FOR FREE the
moment it attaches to a gateway labelled
A ${COMMON_DOMAIN} name does NOT. It needs a
hand-written entry in the k8gb CNAME config, or the
route reports Accepted=True forever and never

g.title: h_k8gb
g.text: cdn.keiretsu.top is delegated to it. One controller
runs in each cluster (three regional controllers;
v1.0.0 intentionally has no leader election).
CoreDNS is three replicas per cluster and is also
exposed through a Tailscale LoadBalancer. A Corefile
resolvable by CNAMEing to the local Envoy tailnet
Service. An ABSENT HTTPRoute reads as healthy, so
an inert route is deployed to every cluster to make

g.title: h_ddns
g.text: current WAN address. Every ExternalDNS CNAME and
every GSLB pool member resolves to that record in

g.title: x_acme
g.text: reached by ACME DNS-01 through the

g.title: x_cert
g.text: Every API token and account key is

g.title: x_auth
g.text: Tinyauth only proves WHO you are, then injects the
Authorization is a separate thing: each protected
route carries its own Envoy SecurityPolicy with
extAuth, defaultAction Deny and an explicit allow-list.
THERE IS NO CENTRAL ROLE MODEL. Access is per-route
and per-person, and visible in the manifest.

g.title: x_borrow
g.text: Robbinsdale and St. Petersburg reach it across the
tailnet rather than running a second copy, so their
protected routes depend on the overlay being up.
Tailnet-only routes lean on tailnet policy instead

g.title: x_tunnel
g.text: an outbound-only tunnel, so that site can publish
without an inbound port forward. A second ingress
path that bypasses the Envoy public tier entirely.
